analyst_view.overall: Mid-table NEC (11th, 14 points) host leaders PSV (26 points) after the international break, with PSV needing a win to stay top; NEC have won their last two (Omonia and Utrecht) and have beaten PSV in two of the last four meetings, with Bryan Linssen (eight goals in 27 games against PSV) playing his 400th Eredivisie match. What changed since this morning: NEC's defence is thinner than thought, as Schreuder told NEC TV he has to 'puzzle' at the back, with Perr Schuurs and Philippe Sandler (setback) out, Deveron Fonville doubtful after returning from Curacao with a knock, and Nuytinck and Mor out (the numbers count only Nuytinck, Mor and Geiger). For PSV, Nagalo, Schouten and Plea are out (counted) plus Ouaissa; Sergino Dest is a question mark after leaving the US camp early, while Paul Wanner trained all week and may make the squad. Referee Jeroen Manschot's above-average card rate is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.1 goals, already including NEC's hot scoring run (14 in six), small cuts for Mor, Geiger and Plea, and a little for the high-scoring head-to-head. What they can't see is that NEC will now be without centre-backs Schuurs and Sandler as well as Nuytinck, with Fonville doubtful too, against PSV's league-best attack; I raise this morning's +3% to +5%, about 4.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners, with NEC's recent corner surge (+2%) and PSV's quieter spell (-5%) already counted. Dest, one of PSV's main crossers, is still a doubt, but Kostic and Perisic should supply width either way and both teams play a similar attacking style, so I stay at 10.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, already pushed up about 18% for referee Jeroen Manschot (3.5 cards a game in 51 games). A patched NEC back line may have to foul more against PSV's runners, but no suspensions hang over either side and there is no special needle, so I stay at 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.4 shots, with NEC's heavy recent shooting (116 in six, +10%) already counted. Schreuder says both teams play in a similar, open way, and PSV's attacking line is close to full strength, which is what the numbers assume, so I stay at about 29.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.0 shots on target, with NEC's sharper recent finishing already in. New since this morning: with Schuurs, Sandler and Nuytinck all out and Fonville doubtful, NEC's makeshift defence is likely to let PSV get more clean shots away than the numbers think, so a mild +3% to about 11.3.
